stages.definition: Dominant step-sign share over nonzero steps; PERSISTENT when share >= 0.75 AND the full-window slope has a nonzero sign.
stages.abstentionSemantics: SHORT_HISTORY only. Data sufficiency and nothing else.
stages.directionDependency: A zero-signed full-window slope yields NOT_PERSISTENT, not abstention.

stages.definition: Bounded-interruption tolerance: PERSISTENT when support or directional consistency clears a candidate threshold and no opposing run exceeds the bound.
stages.abstentionSemantics: THREE reasons: SHORT_OR_MISSING_HISTORY (sufficiency), INDETERMINATE_DIRECTION (dominantSign === 0 || |slope| < .003 || support < .28), CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE (directionalConsistency < .62).
stages.directionDependency: A zero dominant sign or a near-flat slope yields abstention, not an answer.

stages.definition: Composes the STAGE 2I.3 head (BOUNDED_INTERRUPTION_TOLERANCE) into the assembly.
stages.spliceDescription: Wires the Stage 2I.3 head to a corpus carrying the Stage 2I.2 expectation. The head answers INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE where this corpus expects NOT_PERSISTENT, and neither party is internally wrong.

stages.definition: Label schemas only; no persistence implementation.
stages.abstentionSemantics: No abstention label declared in these schemas at all.
stages.note: Three independent stages declare a two-label persistence vocabulary with no INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE member, which is evidence that abstention was not intended as a routine persistence answer.

stages.abstentionSemantics: Recorded as "Emits INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on its own account."
Unchanged. Recorded ABSTENTION_SEMANTICS_DIVERGENCE as the residual defect.

archaeology.gateIntentEvidence: Stage 2I.3 introduced STABLE_NO_TREND and ALTERNATING_DIRECTION families expecting INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE in the same change as the gate. The head and its benchmark agree. No safety rationale, specification comment or documentation for the gate exists in the module.
archaeology.defectOriginEvidence: Stage 2I.4 composes the Stage 2I.3 head with a corpus family carrying the Stage 2I.2 expectation (NOT_PERSISTENT on an alternating series). Every later stage inherited that pairing and scored the mismatch as head error.

semantics.concept: Persistence measures whether a directional tendency, once present, is SUSTAINED across the observation window despite bounded interruption. It is a statement about the window that was supplied, never a prediction.
semantics.persistentDefinition: A single dominant step direction holds across the window, interruptions are bounded (no opposing run longer than the candidate allows), and the window's net movement is consistent with that direction.
semantics.notPersistentDefinition: The window carries enough observations to judge, and no sustained tendency is present. This INCLUDES a flat series (no tendency to sustain), an oscillating or alternating series (a tendency exists but inverts every step, so it is not sustained), a zero-mean noisy series, and a series whose established direction reverses materially before the window ends.
semantics.insufficientEvidenceDefinition: The window does not carry enough observations to judge: fewer than the minimum sample count, or history coverage below the required density. DATA SUFFICIENCY ONLY.
semantics.reversalTreatment: A material reversal inside the window is NOT_PERSISTENT, because the tendency was not sustained to the window's end.
semantics.coreRule: DIRECTION_CERTAINTY and DATA_SUFFICIENCY are different axes. "No stable direction" measured over an adequate window is a POSITIVE FINDING of NOT_PERSISTENT, not an admission that the question could not be answered.
derivedFrom: STAGE2I2 head: abstains on values.length < 6 and on nothing else; a zero-signed slope answers NOT_PERSISTENT.
STAGE2I3 head: its own abstentionReason vocabulary separates SHORT_OR_MISSING_HISTORY from INDETERMINATE_DIRECTION and CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE, marking only the first as a sufficiency failure.
src/experts/oracle.js contract: "when history is too short the expert says so through ORACLE_INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY" — abstention is defined as a history-length concept.
STAGE2I4 assembly: carries a dedicated `abstention` head whose declared role is to be the sufficiency mechanism, which a second in-head sufficiency gate duplicates.
STAGE2L1/2L2/2L4 label schemas: declare a two-label persistence vocabulary with no INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE member.
semantics.notDerivedFrom: No benchmark accuracy figure was consulted in choosing this definition. The definition was fixed before any post-repair accuracy was computed.

axes.question: Are there enough observations, densely enough covered, to answer at all?
Can a single dominant direction be named for the window?
How consistently does the dominant direction hold across steps?
Over how much of the window does it hold?
Does the series alternate on a short period rather than travel?
Does an established direction invert materially before the window ends?
Is step-level variation large relative to net movement?

cases.rationale: Ample data; there is no tendency at all to sustain, which is a finding, not a gap.
Direction inverts every step. Not sustained.
Large amplitude does not make an inverting series sustained.
Zero-mean noise; net movement is nil.
Every step moves the same way. Weak is not the same as unsustained.
Flat steps interleave with rises but nothing opposes the direction.
One excursion is a bounded interruption, which the contract explicitly tolerates.
The tendency was real and then was not sustained to the window end.
Direction turns repeatedly inside the window.
A cycle is the canonical sustained-nothing case.
Decaying amplitude still never sustains a direction.
Growing amplitude is a volatility statement, not a persistence one.
At the minimum the window is sufficient, so an answer is owed.
Below the minimum the window genuinely cannot support an answer. This is the ONLY legitimate abstention in the whole table.

mayAbstainWhen: SHORT_OR_MISSING_HISTORY: fewer than 6 samples, or history coverage below 0.8
mayNotAbstainWhen: INDETERMINATE_DIRECTION: the window is sufficient and the series simply has no dominant direction. That is NOT_PERSISTENT.
underReview: CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE: directional consistency below 0.62 on a sufficient window. Measured and reported here, but NOT changed — the brief asks for the smallest bounded change and the evidence for narrowing this one is weaker.
abstentionContract.principle: Abstention represents insufficient evidence to answer the persistence question, not an inability to assign a direction.

changeDescription: INDETERMINATE_DIRECTION abstention is converted to NOT_PERSISTENT past the head's own sufficiency gate. SHORT_OR_MISSING_HISTORY still abstains; CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE is measured and left unchanged. No threshold, tolerance or PERSISTENT branch is touched, and the frozen module is not edited.

tradeoff.note: A removed abstention counts as a gain only where the case expected an answer and the answer is right. Correct abstentions removed and false assertions introduced are both counted against the change.

residual.cause: The Stage 2L.19 SUSTAINED_RUN family applies jitter on top of a slope as small as 0.004, so on some variants the step signs balance even though the generator intended a sustained ramp. Whether those cases are truly PERSISTENT is a corpus well-posedness question, not a head defect, and this stage does not relabel them: relabelling a case because the head disagrees is exactly the tuning the brief forbids.

interpretation.residualNote: CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE remains an abstention reason on a sufficient window. It is measured and reported but was not narrowed, because the brief asks for the smallest bounded change.

portabilityNote: Stage 2L.10 through 2L.20 remain DIGEST_PRODUCED_SINGLE_PLATFORM. Stage 2L.21 does not change that.
